key_insight: A Bayesian finite element model reconstructs steady vascular velocity and pressure fields from sparse noisy measurements while quantifying uncertainty and enforcing physics.
engineering_relevance: This enables more reliable clinical flow diagnostics by estimating pressure drop, flow rates, and wall shear stress from under-resolved patient-specific data.
method: Represent velocity and pressure with Taylor-Hood finite element basis functions.
Use maximum-entropy physics-informed priors plus a noise-based likelihood to form the posterior.
Compute the MAP via sparse nonlinear least squares, eliminating pressure analytically and using a Laplace approximation for uncertainty.
evidence_signal: On patient-specific cerebral aneurysm, aortic aneurysm, and aortic coarctation cases, the method outperformed tricubic interpolation and matched PINN-level reconstruction accuracy while improving wall shear stress estimates.
watch_item: The approach relies on steady-flow assumptions and a Laplace approximation, so strongly nonlinear or highly unsteady flows may require additional modeling care.
paper_title: Bayesian finite element regression for vascular flow reconstruction with quantified uncertainty
